investigation.title: Swarm Gateway 502 Blocks All Remote Agent Checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime)
investigation.summary: All three remote-agents eval checks (remote-agent-create, remote-agent-state, remote-agent-runtime) failed at 2026-10-12T12:55:54Z with an identical 502 bad_gateway error: the production-api's POST /api/agents call could not reach the swarm gateway ELB at the redacted us-east-2 AWS endpoint. Because the failure occurs before any agent is provisioned, all required evidence (orgId, agentId, vmIdPresent, remoteState) is absent and no contract assertions can be evaluated.
investigation.rootCause: The swarm gateway — the AWS ELB-backed service at http://[REDACTED].elb.us-east-2.amazonaws.com/v1/agents — was unreachable from the production-api at the time of the eval run. The production-api returned HTTP 502 with code "bad_gateway" and the message "swarm gateway unreachable during agent provisioning: error sending request for url (http://[REDACTED].elb.us-east-2.amazonaws.com/v1/agents)". This upstream connectivity failure caused POST /api/agents to fail immediately, preventing agent creation and making all downstream evidence collection impossible. The failure is localized to the swarm gateway dependency of the remote-agents feature; no evidence of a broader production-api outage or user-traffic incident is present in the supplied packet.

If only the eval runner's network path to the production-api was disrupted (e.g., the eval runner's egress IP was blocked), but direct API calls from other clients succeeded, the failure would be isolated to the eval infrastructure rather than the swarm gateway.

If the three sibling checks had different error messages or different HTTP status codes, the shared-dependency hypothesis would be weakened and individual check-level bugs would need to be investigated.

If historical run data showed this 502 pattern recurring intermittently and resolving without intervention, the cause would more likely be transient gateway instability rather than a sustained outage.
